title: Psalms Chapter 110 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 110 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 110 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 110.

questions.question: Who said unto my Lord, "Sit thou at my right hand"?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:1 states, 'The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand...'.

questions.question: According to Psalms 110:1, what will be made thy footstool?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:1 says, '...until I make thine enemies thy footstool.'

questions.question: From where shall the LORD send the rod of thy strength?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:2 says, 'The LORD shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion.'

questions.question: Where does the LORD command to rule according to Psalms 110:2?
options: In the midst of thine enemies
questions.correctAnswer: In the midst of thine enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:2 says, 'rule thou in the midst of thine enemies.'

questions.question: What will thy people be in the day of thy power?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:3 says, 'Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power.'

questions.question: In Psalms 110:3, what is described as coming from the womb of the morning?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:3 says, 'in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning.'

questions.question: What does the Psalm say you have, described as 'the dew'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:3 states, 'thou hast the dew of thy youth.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 110:1 mentions that the LORD will make your enemies your footstool.
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:1 clearly says, 'until I make thine enemies thy footstool.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 110:2 says the rod of strength shall come out of Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:2 specifies the rod of strength comes out of Zion, not Jerusalem.

questions.question: According to Psalms 110:3, when will thy people be willing?
options: In the day of thy power
questions.correctAnswer: In the day of thy power
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:3 states, 'Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power.'

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalms 110 according to the text?
questions.explanation: The title in Psalms 110:1 says, 'A Psalm of David.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 110:3 mentions the 'dew of thy youth.'
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:3 clearly includes the phrase, 'thou hast the dew of thy youth.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 110:2 tells to rule in the midst of thine enemies.
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:2 says, 'rule thou in the midst of thine enemies.'

questions.question: Which comes first in Psalms 110:1-3?
options: The LORD sending the rod of strength out of Zion
The LORD saying, 'Sit thou at my right hand'
Thy people being willing in the day of thy power
Having the dew of thy youth
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD saying, 'Sit thou at my right hand'
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:1 begins with the LORD saying 'Sit thou at my right hand', before the other events in verses 2 and 3.

questions.question: In Psalms 110:1, who is addressed as 'my Lord'?
questions.explanation: Though the verse says 'my Lord,' the traditional understanding is that it refers to the Messiah; the text states 'The LORD said unto my Lord' indicating distinction between the LORD and this Lord (Psalms 110:1).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 110 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 110 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 110:4, what has the LORD sworn regarding the priesthood?
options: The priesthood will end with Aaron's descendants
You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek
The priesthood is temporary and will be replaced
questions.correctAnswer: You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:4 states that the LORD has sworn an unchangeable oath that the person addressed is a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek, highlighting an eternal priesthood distinct from the Levitical line.

questions.question: How does Psalms 110:5 describe the Lord's action at the right hand of the one addressed?
options: He will bless the nations with peace
He shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath
He will judge the poor with mercy
He will build a temple for the people
questions.correctAnswer: He shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath
questions.explanation: Verse 5 clearly states that the Lord at the right hand will strike through kings during His wrath, showing divine authority and judgment over earthly rulers.

questions.question: What is promised in Psalms 110:6 about judgment among the heathen?
options: He will judge with mercy and kindness
He shall fill the places with the dead bodies and wound many heads
He will establish peace among the nations
He will ignore the heathen completely
questions.correctAnswer: He shall fill the places with the dead bodies and wound many heads
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:6 describes a severe judgment where the Lord will fill places with dead bodies and wound the heads over many countries, indicating a decisive victory over enemies.

questions.question: How does Psalms 110:4-6 together teach about God’s faithfulness and judgment?
options: God changes His mind frequently about His promises
God’s oath about priesthood leads to His active judgment over kings and nations
God only judges based on human traditions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s oath about priesthood leads to His active judgment over kings and nations
questions.explanation: Verses 4 through 6 show that because God has sworn an unchangeable oath concerning the priesthood (v.4), He actively exercises judgment by striking kings and judging heathen nations (vv.5-6), demonstrating faithfulness and power.

questions.question: What biblical virtue can believers learn from the Lord reigning at the right hand and striking kings, as in Psalms 110:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:5 illustrates God's sovereign power to judge kings, teaching believers to trust God’s justice rather than seeking personal vengeance or pride.

questions.question: According to Psalms 110:6, what will happen to the leaders of many countries?
options: They will be exalted by God
questions.explanation: Verse 6 specifically states that 'he shall wound the heads over many countries,' indicating divine judgment against leaders of multiple nations.

questions.question: What assurance does Psalms 110:4 give about God's promises?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:4 says the LORD hath sworn and will not repent, assuring believers of the certainty and unchangeability of His promises.

questions.question: How does Psalms 110:7 teach believers about humility in times of rest or refreshment?
options: It shows that even after refreshment, one must remain humble and lifted in spirit
It teaches ignoring times of rest
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that even after refreshment, one must remain humble and lifted in spirit
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says 'He shall drink of the brook in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head,' teaching that after receiving refreshment, one should remain confident and humble, trusting God’s provision.

questions.question: A brother in Christ feels overwhelmed by opposition. Based on Psalms 110:2-3, what biblical truth can encourage him?
options: God sends strength and willing people to support him in the day of power
He must fight enemies alone without help
Opposition means God has abandoned him
He should avoid all conflict at any cost
questions.correctAnswer: God sends strength and willing people to support him in the day of power
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:2-3 promises that God sends strength from Zion and that people will be willing in the day of power, assuring believers they are not alone in opposition.

questions.question: What can believers learn about integrity from Psalms 110:4-6?
options: God’s unchanging oath demands faithful obedience and trust
One should depend on human strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: God’s unchanging oath demands faithful obedience and trust
questions.explanation: The LORD’s oath in verse 4 and His active judgment in verses 5-6 teach that God’s promises are reliable, encouraging believers to live with integrity and trust in Him.

questions.question: What does Psalms 110:6 imply about the consequences of disobedience to God?
options: Severe judgment and defeat for nations opposing God
questions.correctAnswer: Severe judgment and defeat for nations opposing God
questions.explanation: Verse 6 describes how God will judge among the heathen and fill places with dead bodies, indicating that disobedience leads to serious consequences.

questions.question: How do Psalms 110:5 and 110:6 together illustrate God’s role in leadership and justice?
options: God actively executes justice by striking kings and judging nations
God delegates judgment entirely to humans
questions.correctAnswer: God actively executes justice by striking kings and judging nations
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows God striking kings, and verse 6 shows Him judging nations, indicating His active and sovereign role in leadership and justice.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 110:4 teaches that the priesthood of Melchizedek’s order is temporary.
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states that the priesthood is forever after the order of Melchizedek, emphasizing its eternal nature, not temporary.

questions.question: How does Psalms 110:7 encourage believers about God’s provision during difficult journeys?
options: They will be refreshed and strengthened to continue confidently
They must rely only on human resources
questions.correctAnswer: They will be refreshed and strengthened to continue confidently
questions.explanation: Verse 7 uses the imagery of drinking from a brook and lifting up the head, symbolizing God’s provision and renewed strength during trials.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 110:5 teaches that the Lord will strike kings gently and with mercy.
questions.explanation: Verse 5 specifies that the Lord shall strike through kings in the day of His wrath, indicating a strong and decisive judgment rather than gentle mercy.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 110 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 110.

questions.question: According to Psalms 110:7, what action leads to 'therefore shall he lift up the head'?
options: He shall drink of the brook in the way
He shall judge among the heathen
He shall send the rod of strength
questions.correctAnswer: He shall drink of the brook in the way
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:7 says that 'He shall drink of the brook in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head,' indicating that drinking from the brook causes the lifting up of the head.

questions.question: Which Old Testament figure's priestly order is the psalmist referring to in Psalms 110:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:4 explicitly states, 'Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek,' referring to Melchizedek's priestly order.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'right hand' mentioned multiple times in Psalms 110 (e.g. verse 1 and 5)?
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern culture, including Psalms 110:1 and 110:5, the 'right hand' symbolizes a place of power and honor, indicating authority given by the LORD.

questions.question: In Psalms 110:6, what is the described role of the Lord at the right hand?
options: He shall judge among the heathen and fill places with dead bodies
He shall sing praises among the people
He shall build temples in foreign lands
He shall bless the nations with peace
questions.correctAnswer: He shall judge among the heathen and fill places with dead bodies
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:6 describes the Lord at the right hand judging the heathen and filling places with dead bodies, indicating judgment and victory over enemies.

questions.question: Which New Testament book quotes Psalms 110:1 as a proof of Jesus’ exalted position?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:34-35 quotes Psalms 110:1 to affirm Jesus’ exalted position at the right hand of God, showing a fulfillment of this Psalm in the New Testament.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'until I make thine enemies thy footstool' in Psalms 110:1 symbolize?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 110:1, making enemies a footstool symbolizes total victory and subjugation, a common ancient Near Eastern metaphor for dominance.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 110:3 describes the people as reluctant and fearful in the day of power.
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:3 says, 'Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power,' indicating willingness, not reluctance or fear.

questions.question: How does Psalms 110:4’s designation of the priesthood after the order of Melchizedek connect to the New Testament?
options: It foreshadows Jesus’ eternal priesthood as described in Hebrews
It refers only to Old Testament priests
It predicts the end of priesthood
It relates to Levitical priests exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Jesus’ eternal priesthood as described in Hebrews
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7 references Psalms 110:4 to explain Jesus’ eternal priesthood after Melchizedek’s order, showing typology and fulfillment.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in the structure of Psalms 110, especially in the first and last verses?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110 uses inclusio by beginning and ending with imagery of exaltation—the right hand and lifting up the head—framing the whole Psalm.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'rod' in Psalms 110:2 signify in ancient Near Eastern royal symbolism?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'rod' (shebet) in Psalms 110:2 represents a scepter, a common symbol of royal authority and ruling power in the ancient Near East.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 110 portrays the Messiah only as a king with no priestly function.
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:4 clearly portrays the Messiah as both king and priest, 'a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek,' indicating dual roles.

questions.question: Psalms 110:5 mentions 'The Lord at thy right hand shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath.' Which New Testament passage echoes this imagery of divine judgment?
questions.explanation: Revelation 19:15 depicts Christ striking the nations with a sharp sword from His mouth in wrath, paralleling Psalms 110:5’s imagery of divine judgment against kings.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the dew of thy youth' in Psalms 110:3?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 110:3, 'dew of thy youth' symbolizes freshness and vitality, highlighting blessing and renewal.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event or figure is often considered a typological precursor to the priest-king described in Psalms 110?
questions.explanation: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest, is the archetype for the priest-king in Psalms 110, serving as a type fulfilled in the Messiah.

questions.question: In Psalms 110:2, what is the role of the 'rod of thy strength' sent out of Zion?
options: To rule in the midst of enemies
questions.correctAnswer: To rule in the midst of enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:2 states the LORD will send the rod of strength from Zion to rule among enemies, signifying divine authority and conquest.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 110 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 110 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 110:1 indicate about the position of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:1 states that the LORD said unto my Lord, 'Sit thou at my right hand', indicating a position of authority and honor.

questions.question: According to Psalms 110:2, where will the rod of strength be sent from?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:2 mentions that 'The LORD shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion', indicating that Zion is the source of strength.

questions.question: What does Psalms 110:4 reveal about the nature of the priesthood mentioned?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:4 specifies that the priesthood is 'for ever after the order of Melchizedek', indicating its eternal and distinct nature.

questions.question: What is promised in the day of power according to Psalms 110:3?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 110:3, it states 'Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power', indicating a response of willingness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 110:5 describe the Lord doing at thy right hand?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:5 states that 'The Lord at thy right hand shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath', depicting divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Psalms 110:6, what will happen among the heathen?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:6 declares 'He shall judge among the heathen', indicating God's authority over all peoples.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated in Psalms 110:4 regarding His promises?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:4 shows God's faithfulness as He 'hath sworn, and will not repent', indicating His unchanging nature.

questions.question: What does Psalms 110:7 imply about the Lord's sustenance?
options: He shall drink of the brook
questions.correctAnswer: He shall drink of the brook
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:7 states 'He shall drink of the brook in the way', which implies divine sustenance and provision.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 110:2 and 110:6 convey about God's rule?
options: He rules from Zion but spares the wicked
He rules powerfully and judges the wicked
He rules with peace and mercy
questions.correctAnswer: He rules powerfully and judges the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:2 speaks of ruling 'in the midst of thine enemies', while 110:6 describes judging among the heathen, emphasizing God's power.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'dew of thy youth' in Psalms 110:3 suggest about the nature of the ruler?
questions.explanation: The 'dew of thy youth' in Psalms 110:3 indicates vitality and freshness, suggesting a ruler with renewed strength.

questions.question: According to Psalms 110:6, what will happen to the heads over many countries?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:6 states 'he shall wound the heads over many countries', indicating a forceful divine judgment.

questions.question: What does Psalms 110:1 reflect about the relationship between the LORD and David's Lord?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:1 presents a conversation between the LORD and David's Lord, indicating a hierarchy in authority.

questions.question: What does Psalms 110:5 imply about the nature of divine wrath?
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:5 indicates that divine wrath is directed, as the Lord will strike through kings, signifying intentional judgment.

questions.question: What does Psalms 110:7 illustrate about the victorious ruler's actions?
options: He will lift up his head
questions.correctAnswer: He will lift up his head
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:7 states that 'therefore shall he lift up the head', indicating a posture of victory and confidence.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the concept of a priesthood after Melchizedek is confusing and unnecessary. What does Psalms 110:4 actually teach?
options: It is limited to one tribe
questions.explanation: Psalms 110:4 teaches that 'Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek', indicating its unique and eternal nature, fulfilling a significant role in God's plan.
